title: Super Bowl Monday Hangover: Game-Day Plan and Next-Day Fixes
excerpt: Why the Monday after the Super Bowl hits so hard, a quarter-by-quarter plan to drink smarter at the party, and how to get through the workday if you wake up hungover.
metaDescription: Why the Monday after the Super Bowl hurts, a quarter-by-quarter plan to pace your drinking, and how to get through the workday if you wake up hungover.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** the Super Bowl Monday hangover is mostly a scheduling problem. The game kicks off around 6:30 p.m. Eastern on a Sunday, the parties start hours earlier, the drinks are mostly beer and the food is mostly salt and fat, and the night ends late with a work or school morning a few hours away. You get a long drinking session, short sleep, and no recovery day. The good news is that the same schedule makes it easy to plan around: eat before the pregame, pace yourself by quarters, switch to water by the fourth quarter, and set up Monday morning before you go to bed.

**If you came here for the football meaning:** a "Super Bowl hangover" is also the sports term for a team that wins (or loses) the big game and then struggles the following season. We cover that briefly below, but this guide is mostly about the other kind, the one you wake up with on Monday.

> **When to see a doctor (or call 911).** Most game-day hangovers are miserable but harmless, and they fade within a day. Get medical help if someone at the party **can't be woken up, is breathing slowly or irregularly, has blue or pale skin, is having a seizure, or keeps vomiting while confused**. Those are signs of alcohol poisoning, and you should call 911 rather than let them "sleep it off." The next day, see a doctor if you **can't keep fluids down for most of the day, vomit blood, have severe belly pain, feel confused, or have chest pain or a racing heart that won't settle**. If you notice shaking, sweating, or anxiety that gets worse instead of better as the day goes on and you drink most days, tell a doctor. That can be a sign your body has come to depend on alcohol, and it's worth getting checked, not toughing out. This article is general information, not medical advice.

## What "Super Bowl Hangover" Means in Football

Sportswriters use "Super Bowl hangover" to describe a team that has a disappointing season right after playing in the Super Bowl. It's used for winners and, maybe even more often, for losers. The theory is that a deep playoff run means a longer season, more injuries, less rest, a shorter offseason, players getting paid or leaving in free agency, and coaches getting hired away. Add in a harder schedule the next year and the fact that every opponent gets up to play the champion, and a dip seems reasonable.

Whether the effect is real or just regression to the mean (teams that had an unusually great year tend to look more ordinary the next one) is an argument sports analysts have every year. Some teams have repeated as champions or returned to the game the next season, and others have collapsed. We're a hangover-science site, not a football analytics site, so we'll leave the debate there. The rest of this guide is about the hangover that has a physical cause.

## Why the Monday After the Super Bowl Hits So Hard

A Super Bowl party stacks almost every known hangover risk into one evening. None of them is unusual on its own. The combination is what makes Monday rough.

### 1. It's a long session that starts in daylight

Many parties start in the afternoon with the pregame show, and the game itself, with halftime and commercials, runs for around four hours. That can mean six or seven hours of drinking. Long sessions add up to more total drinks than people realize, because nobody is counting during a close third quarter. If your party starts early, our guide to [day drinking](/never-hungover/day-drinking) covers why afternoon starts tend to sneak up on people.

### 2. The drink is mostly beer, and beer is easy to keep drinking

Beer has less alcohol per ounce than wine or spirits, which makes it feel harmless. But a 12-ounce beer at about 5% alcohol is one standard drink, and many craft beers and IPAs run 7% to 9%, which makes each can closer to one and a half or two drinks. Beer is also cold, fizzy, and refilled constantly at a party. For more on why beer hangovers have their own feel (the bloating, the volume, the carbonation), see our [beer hangover guide](/never-hungover/beer-hangover).

### 3. The food is salty, and salt makes you thirsty

Wings, chips, pretzels, nachos, pizza, and chili are the standard spread. Fatty food in your stomach slows how fast alcohol is absorbed, which is genuinely helpful. The catch is the salt. Salty snacks make you thirsty, and at a Super Bowl party the nearest drink is usually another beer, not a glass of water. Alcohol also makes you pee more, so you can end the night both full and dehydrated.

### 4. The night ends late and Monday starts early

The game usually ends somewhere around 10 p.m. Eastern, and later if it goes to overtime. Then there's the post-game talk, the cleanup, and the drive or ride home. On the West Coast the timing is easier, but in the East and Central time zones many people get to bed close to midnight or later with an alarm set for 6 or 7. Alcohol also breaks up your sleep in the second half of the night, so even the hours you get aren't restful. Short, broken sleep is one of the biggest drivers of how bad a hangover feels. Our guide to [why you can't sleep after drinking](/never-hungover/cant-sleep-after-drinking) explains what alcohol does to your sleep cycle.

### 5. There's no recovery day

New Year's Day and the Fourth of July give you room to recover. Super Bowl Monday is a regular workday for most people. The hangover is the same, but you have to function through it, which makes it feel worse.

### 6. Emotions and adrenaline

A close game means a lot of shouting, standing, and stress. If your team lost, you may also wake up feeling flat or anxious. There's no good evidence that losing makes a hangover physically worse, but the low mood and anxiety many people feel the day after drinking (often called "hangxiety") can stack on top of disappointment. Our [hangxiety guide](/never-hungover/hangxiety-complete-guide-2026-supplements-research) covers what's behind that feeling.

## How to Prevent a Super Bowl Monday Hangover: A Game Plan by Quarter

The only thing that reliably prevents a hangover is drinking less. Everything else reduces the damage. The structure of a football game happens to give you natural checkpoints, so use them.

### Before kickoff: eat a real meal

Don't arrive hungry and plan to eat wings. Have a proper meal with protein and some carbohydrates a few hours before you start drinking. Food in your stomach slows how quickly alcohol reaches your bloodstream, which flattens the spike in your blood alcohol and makes it easier to stay in control of the pace. Drink a big glass of water before you leave the house.

If you're hosting, put out real food at the start, not just chips. A pot of chili, a tray of sandwiches, or a pasta dish gives people something substantial before the beer adds up.

### First quarter: set your number and your pace

Decide roughly how many drinks you're going to have before the game starts. A useful rule of thumb is no more than one standard drink per hour, with a glass of water in between. Your liver clears about one standard drink an hour, give or take, so drinking faster than that means alcohol builds up in your blood.

Some practical tricks:

- **Pick a lower-alcohol beer.** A light beer around 4% gives you the ritual of holding a beer with less alcohol per can than a 7% IPA.
- **Use a smaller glass or a can, not a pitcher.** It's easier to count cans.
- **Alternate with a non-alcoholic option.** Many non-alcoholic beers taste close enough to the real thing to keep you in the spirit of the party.
- **Don't do drinking games.** "Drink every time they say [the quarterback's name]" is how a party turns into a lost Monday.

### Halftime: the reset

Halftime is your natural break. Drink a full glass of water, eat something, and take stock. If you're already past the number you planned, the second half is a good time to slow down rather than catch up.

### Third quarter: keep the water going

This is often when people lose count. The game is tense, the commercials are on, and the cooler is right there. Keep a water bottle next to your beer and finish a few sips every time you open a new can.

### Fourth quarter: switch off

Try to have your last alcoholic drink before the fourth quarter starts, or at least before the final two minutes. That gives your body more time to process alcohol before you sleep, and it means you're less likely to be impaired when you head home. Switch to water, seltzer, or a non-alcoholic beer for the finish.

### After the final whistle: set up Monday morning

Before bed:

- **Drink a glass or two of water**, but don't force a huge amount. You'll just be up all night.
- **Put water and a snack next to your bed.**
- **Set out what you need for the morning**: clothes, bag, coffee ready to brew.
- **Skip the late-night painkiller.** Don't take acetaminophen (Tylenol) "just in case" while alcohol is still in your system. More on painkillers below.

For a fuller rundown of habits with the best evidence, see our [guide to preventing a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) and our [party drinking tips](/never-hungover/party-drinking-tips). Super Bowl Sunday is one of the heaviest drinking days of the year in the US; our list of the [biggest drinking days of the year](/never-hungover/biggest-drinking-days-of-the-year) shows where it ranks.

## Game-Day Food: What Helps and What Doesn't

Food doesn't absorb alcohol like a sponge, but it does slow how fast alcohol leaves your stomach for your small intestine, where most of it is absorbed. That gives your liver more time to keep up. Here's how the typical Super Bowl spread stacks up:

| Food | Helps | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| Wings | Protein and fat slow absorption | Very salty, especially with hot sauce and dry rubs; spicy sauces can irritate a stomach already upset by alcohol |
| Chili | Protein, fiber, and a real meal's worth of calories | Spicy versions and beans can add to bloating and gas the next morning |
| Pizza | Carbohydrates and fat | Salty; easy to eat late at night instead of early |
| Chips, pretzels, nachos | Something in your stomach | Lots of salt with little protein, which drives thirst |
| Guacamole, veggie trays | Water, fiber, and potassium | Usually the most ignored part of the table |
| Sliders, sandwiches | Protein and carbohydrates together | Fine; just eat them early |

The best approach is to eat most of your food in the first half of the party, not after the game. A plate of wings at 11 p.m. doesn't do much for the beer you drank at 4.

## The Monday Morning Recovery Playbook

If you wake up hungover anyway, there's no cure, but there are ways to make the morning more manageable. Most hangovers clear within about 24 hours, so the goal is to get through the workday. Our guide to [how long a hangover lasts](/never-hungover/how-long-does-hangover-last) explains the usual timeline. For how hangovers affect focus and performance on the job, see our guide to [hangovers and your career](/never-hungover/hangover-career-impact-dhm-solution-2025).

### Rehydrate steadily

Start with a glass of water as soon as you wake up, then keep sipping through the morning. If you feel especially drained, a drink with electrolytes (sodium and potassium) can help your body hold onto the fluid. Sports drinks and oral rehydration drinks both work; our [Gatorade for hangover](/never-hungover/gatorade-for-hangover) page compares the options. You don't need to chug. Steady sipping is easier on a queasy stomach.

### Eat breakfast, even a small one

Alcohol can lower your blood sugar, which adds to the shaky, weak, foggy feeling. A simple breakfast with some protein and carbohydrates, like eggs on toast, oatmeal with a banana, or yogurt and fruit, helps. If your stomach is upset, start bland with toast or crackers. For ideas, see our [best hangover breakfast guide](/never-hungover/best-hangover-breakfast), or if you're grabbing something on the way to work, our [fast food for hangovers](/never-hungover/best-fast-food-for-hangover) roundup.

### Coffee: yes, but not a pot of it

A cup or two of coffee can take the edge off the grogginess, and if you drink coffee every day, skipping it can add a caffeine-withdrawal headache on top of your hangover. Just don't overdo it. Too much caffeine on an empty, irritated stomach can make nausea and jitteriness worse. Drink water alongside it.

### Painkillers: pick carefully

- **Ibuprofen or naproxen** can help a headache and muscle aches. Take it with food and water, since alcohol already irritates your stomach lining, and these drugs can too. Skip them if you have stomach ulcers, kidney problems, or take blood thinners, unless your doctor has said otherwise.
- **Acetaminophen (Tylenol)** is processed by the liver, the same organ that just spent the night on alcohol. A single normal dose the morning after a party is unlikely to harm a healthy adult who doesn't drink heavily day to day, but don't take it while alcohol is still in your system and never go over the label limit. Watch for acetaminophen hidden in cold and flu products. Our [Tylenol and alcohol guide](/never-hungover/tylenol-and-alcohol) explains the risks in detail.
- If you're not sure which to take, our [Advil or Tylenol for a hangover](/never-hungover/advil-or-tylenol-for-hangover) page compares them.

### Skip the hair of the dog

A morning beer can delay how you feel by putting more alcohol in your blood, but it just pushes the hangover later into the day and adds to the total. There is no good evidence that it helps you recover. It's also a bad idea before work. Our [hair of the dog guide](/never-hungover/does-hair-of-the-dog-work) explains why it seems to work for a little while.

### Move a little, nap if you can

A short walk outside and some daylight can make you feel more awake. Don't plan a hard workout. If you can grab a 20-minute nap at lunch, it can help, since short sleep is a big part of the Monday misery. Our guide on [whether sleep helps a hangover](/never-hungover/does-sleep-help-a-hangover) covers how to time it.

## Driving the Morning After: Check Before You Go

This is the part of Super Bowl Monday people underestimate. If you drank heavily and late on Sunday, you may still have alcohol in your blood when you get up for work on Monday. Your body clears roughly one standard drink per hour, and nothing (coffee, a cold shower, a big breakfast) speeds that up. Ten drinks finished at 11 p.m. can still be in your system at 7 a.m.

Even once your blood alcohol is back to zero, a hangover itself can affect driving. Driving-simulator studies by hangover researchers in the Netherlands have found that people with a hangover and no alcohol left in their blood drove less steadily than when they were rested and sober, with impairment in some cases comparable to driving after drinking. Tiredness from short sleep adds to it.

What that means in practice:

- If you drank a lot late on Sunday, don't assume you're fine to drive at 7 a.m. Take a ride share, transit, or a later start if you can.
- If you feel foggy, slow, or exhausted, treat that as a reason not to drive, even if you think the alcohol is gone.
- Plan your ride home from the party before you start drinking.

Our guides on [driving hungover](/never-hungover/driving-hungover) and [how long to wait after drinking to drive](/never-hungover/how-long-after-drinking-can-you-drive) go into the details.

## Getting Through the Workday

You can't fully fix a hangover by 9 a.m., but you can make the day easier:

- **Front-load the easy tasks.** Answer emails and do routine work in the morning, and save anything that needs careful thinking for the afternoon, when most people feel noticeably better.
- **Keep water at your desk** and refill it every time you get up.
- **Eat lunch.** A real lunch helps more than a vending-machine snack.
- **Avoid big decisions or difficult conversations** if you can push them a day.
- **If you work a safety-sensitive job** (driving, machinery, healthcare, construction), be honest with yourself about whether you're fit to work. Being hungover around heavy equipment is a real hazard.

People joke about the Monday after the Super Bowl being an unofficial holiday, and every year there's talk of calling in sick or taking a personal day. If you can schedule a day off or a late start in advance, that's the most reliable hangover plan of all. If you can't, the steps above make the day survivable.

## If You're Hosting the Party

Hosts can make the Monday after easier for everyone:

- **Serve real food early**, not just snacks.
- **Put out water and non-alcoholic drinks** where people can see them, not hidden in the garage fridge. A tub of seltzer next to the beer gets used.
- **Offer a lower-alcohol beer option.**
- **Close the bar at the start of the fourth quarter** and bring out dessert and coffee instead.
- **Help guests get home safely.** Have ride-share numbers handy, offer a couch, and take keys from anyone who shouldn't drive.
- **Know the signs of alcohol poisoning** (listed in the box at the top). If a guest can't be woken, is breathing slowly, or is vomiting while confused, call 911 and don't leave them alone. Lay them on their side so they won't choke if they vomit.

## Does Losing Make Your Hangover Worse?

Plenty of fans swear Monday is worse after a loss. There's no good evidence that disappointment changes how your body processes alcohol. But the things that tend to come with a loss can make you feel worse: drinking faster in a frustrating second half, staying up later to rehash it, and waking up already in a bad mood. Low mood and anxiety are part of many hangovers anyway, so a loss can amplify a feeling that was already there. If your team won, you might have celebrated harder and longer, which brings its own Monday. Either way, the fix is the same: pace, water, food, and sleep.

## What About Hangover Supplements?

Some people take a supplement before or during a big party. Here's an honest view.

**Electrolyte drinks** won't prevent a hangover, but they can help with the dehydrated, drained feeling, especially if you sweated a lot or didn't drink much water. Our [electrolytes and alcohol guide](/never-hungover/electrolytes-and-alcohol) covers when they're worth it.

**DHM (dihydromyricetin)** is a plant compound from the Japanese raisin tree that's often sold for hangovers. Most of the research comes from animal and lab studies, which suggest it may affect how the body handles alcohol and may support the liver. Human evidence is limited and mixed. There is no good evidence that DHM prevents hangovers, and it does nothing about the short sleep, the salt, or the volume of beer. If you want to try it for a big game, take it as directed on the label, keep your expectations realistic, and treat it as an add-on to pacing and water, not a replacement. Popular options include [No Days Wasted DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) and the lower-cost [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20). Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) explains timing, and our [supplement reviews](/reviews) compare the main brands.

If you take prescription medication, check with a pharmacist before adding any supplement.

## The Bottom Line

- The Super Bowl Monday hangover comes from a long session, lots of beer, salty food, a late night, and a workday the next morning.
- Eat a real meal before the pregame, aim for about one drink an hour with water in between, use halftime as a reset, and stop drinking by the fourth quarter.
- Before bed, drink some water, set up your morning, and skip the "just in case" Tylenol.
- On Monday, sip water or an electrolyte drink, eat breakfast, keep coffee moderate, and choose painkillers carefully.
- Don't assume you're fit to drive Monday morning after a heavy, late night.
- If someone at the party can't be woken or is breathing slowly, call 911.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is a Super Bowl hangover in football?**

In football, a "Super Bowl hangover" is a nickname for a team that has a disappointing season right after playing in the Super Bowl. People blame a longer season, injuries, a shorter offseason, roster changes, and a tougher schedule. Analysts disagree about how real the effect is, and some of it may just be teams returning to normal after an unusually good year. Outside of sports, the phrase usually means the hangover people wake up with on the Monday after the game.

**How do I avoid a hangover after the Super Bowl?**

Drinking less is the only thing that reliably works. Beyond that, eat a real meal before you start, aim for about one standard drink per hour with a glass of water in between, choose lower-alcohol beer, use halftime to eat and drink water, and stop drinking by the start of the fourth quarter. Before bed, have some water and get your morning ready so you can sleep as long as possible.

**Why is the Monday after the Super Bowl so bad?**

It combines several hangover risks at once: a long drinking session that often starts in the afternoon, mostly beer, salty food that makes you thirsty, a late finish in Eastern and Central time zones, broken sleep from alcohol, and a regular workday the next morning with no time to recover.

**Is it safe to drive the morning after a Super Bowl party?**

Not always. Your body clears roughly one standard drink an hour, so after a heavy, late night you may still have alcohol in your blood on Monday morning. Even after it's gone, driving-simulator studies suggest a hangover itself can make driving less safe, and short sleep adds to that. If you drank heavily or feel foggy and slow, take a ride share or transit, or start later.

**What should I eat at a Super Bowl party to avoid a hangover?**

Eat a balanced meal before you start, then focus on protein and real food early in the party: chili, sliders, sandwiches, and wings. Food slows how fast alcohol is absorbed. Go easy on chips, pretzels, and very salty snacks, which make you thirsty, and drink water alongside them. Eating a big plate late at night does much less than eating early.

**What's the fastest way to get over a hangover on Monday morning?**

There's no quick cure, and most hangovers fade within about 24 hours. To make the morning easier, sip water or an electrolyte drink, eat a simple breakfast with protein and carbohydrates, have a cup or two of coffee if you normally drink it, and take ibuprofen with food if you need it for a headache. Avoid a morning beer, which only delays the hangover.

**Can I take Tylenol after a Super Bowl party?**

A single normal dose the next morning is unlikely to harm a healthy adult who doesn't drink heavily day to day, but don't take it before bed while alcohol is still in your system, never exceed the label limit, and check other products for hidden acetaminophen. If you have three or more drinks most days or have liver problems, ask a doctor or pharmacist first.

**Does DHM help with a Super Bowl hangover?**

There is no good evidence that DHM prevents hangovers. Most research on it comes from animal and lab studies, with limited human data. Some people use it as an add-on before a big night, but it doesn't make up for drinking a lot, eating salty food, or sleeping four hours. Pacing yourself, drinking water, and eating well matter far more.
